# ASVS 5.0.0 L2: V7 Session Management

<!-- Generated by `pnpm security:asvs --write` from the YAML file next to this one. Do not edit by hand. -->

> Self-assessment against OWASP ASVS 5.0.0, Level 2, chapter V7 Session Management: not yet assessed by a person. The entries below are the working state, filled in with tests and code pointers; the maintainer's first pass and second pass are still to come. This is not a certification, and no independent party has reviewed it. OWASP does not certify projects.

Status: **in progress**. 8 pass, 0 n/a, 10 fail.

| Requirement | Level | Status | Evidence | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **7.1.1** Verify that the user's session inactivity timeout and absolute maximum session lifetime are documented, are appropriate in combination with other controls, and that the documentation includes justification for any deviations from NIST SP 800-63B re-authentication requirements. | L2 | fail |  | Not met. The 7-day sliding inactivity rule is in modules/core-identity/README.md and ADR-0007, but no absolute maximum lifetime exists or is documented, and there is no justification against NIST SP 800-63B. Tracked in #9007. |
| **7.1.2** Verify that the documentation defines how many concurrent (parallel) sessions are allowed for one account as well as the intended behaviors and actions to be taken when the maximum number of active sessions is reached. | L2 | fail |  | Not met. Nothing documents how many concurrent sessions an account may have or what happens at the limit; the code has no limit. Tracked in #9007. |
| **7.1.3** Verify that all systems that create and manage user sessions as part of a federated identity management ecosystem (such as SSO systems) are documented along with controls to coordinate session lifetimes, termination, and any other conditions that require re-authentication. | L2 | fail |  | Not met. OIDC sign-in creates an independent local session and the identity provider is not consulted afterwards; no document says how session lifetimes and termination are coordinated. Tracked in #9007. |
| **7.2.1** Verify that the application performs all session token verification using a trusted, backend service. | L1 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.2.1]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts) | Every request is checked against identity_session by the SHA-256 of the cookie value; nothing is verified in the browser. A 5 s per-process cache is the documented staleness bound (ADR-0007). |
| **7.2.2** Verify that the application uses either self-contained or reference tokens that are dynamically generated for session management, i.e. not using static API secrets and keys. | L1 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.2.2]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/session-id.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/session-id.ts) | A new random reference token is made for every login; no static API secret serves as a session. |
| **7.2.3** Verify that if reference tokens are used to represent user sessions, they are unique and generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) and possess at least 128 bits of entropy. | L1 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.2.3]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/session-id.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/session-id.ts) | randomBytes(32) from node:crypto (CSPRNG), 256 bits, unique index on the hash. The test shows length and uniqueness; the CSPRNG claim rests on the code. |
| **7.2.4** Verify that the application generates a new session token on user authentication, including re-authentication, and terminates the current session token. | L1 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.2.4]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/accounts.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/accounts.ts) | Password login and OIDC login each make a new server-generated id and end the session the browser presented. |
| **7.3.1** Verify that there is an inactivity timeout such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions. | L2 | fail |  | Not met yet. The 7-day inactivity timeout is enforced (sessions.resolve) and is a documented decision (ADR-0007), but the requirement asks for re-authentication according to a risk analysis, and none is written (see 7.1.1). Becomes a pass once 7.1.1 documents the analysis. Tracked in #9007. |
| **7.3.2** Verify that there is an absolute maximum session lifetime such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions. | L2 | fail |  | Not met (code gap). Every use after 60 s sets expiresAt = now + 7 days and createdAt is never consulted, so a session that is used often never expires. Own issue #9101. |
| **7.4.1** Verify that when session termination is triggered (such as logout or expiration), the application disallows any further use of the session. For reference tokens or stateful sessions, this means invalidating the session data at the application backend. Applications using self-contained tokens will need a solution such as maintaining a list of terminated tokens, disallowing tokens produced before a per-user date and time or rotating a per-user signing key. | L1 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.4.1]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts) | Logout, log out everywhere and expiry delete or stop the row; other server processes may accept a revoked session for at most the 5 s cache TTL (ADR-0007). |
| **7.4.2** Verify that the application terminates all active sessions when a user account is disabled or deleted (such as an employee leaving the company). | L1 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.4.2]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts)<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/approval.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/approval.ts) | sessions.resolve refuses a session whose user is not active or is deleted, on every uncached lookup; rejecting a user revokes all their sessions. The rows of a deleted user stay and the 5 s cache is not dropped. No disable-account feature exists yet (backlog); when it does it must call revokeAll and get its own test. A reviewer may judge "refused" weaker than "terminated". |
| **7.4.3** Verify that the application gives the option to terminate all other active sessions after a successful change or removal of any authentication factor (including password change via reset or recovery and, if present, an MFA settings update). | L2 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.4.3]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/recovery.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/recovery.ts) | A password change or reset ends every session; stricter than an option. There is no MFA to change. Linking an OIDC identity does not end other sessions. |
| **7.4.4** Verify that all pages that require authentication have easy and visible access to logout functionality. | L2 | fail |  | Not met yet. The logout API exists (POST /auth/logout) but apps/web has no authenticated page and no logout control until M5. Re-assess with a Playwright test when the UI lands. Tracked in #9007. |
| **7.4.5** Verify that application administrators are able to terminate active sessions for an individual user or for all users. | L2 | fail |  | Not met (code gap). No route lets an administrator end the sessions of one user or of all users; POST /auth/logout-all ends only the caller's own (defect-01 test proves it). Listed in docs/backlog.md. Own issue #9102. |
| **7.5.1** Verify that the application requires full re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes which may affect authentication such as email address, phone number, MFA configuration, or other information used in account recovery. | L2 | fail |  | Not met (code gap). A password change asks for the current password, but changing the email address (PATCH /account/profile) or linking an OIDC identity needs only the session. Own issue #9103. |
| **7.5.2** Verify that users are able to view and (having authenticated again with at least one factor) terminate any or all currently active sessions. | L2 | fail |  | Not met (code gap). Users can end all their sessions (POST /auth/logout-all, no re-authentication) but cannot list them or end one; identity_session stores no device data. Own issue #9104. |
| **7.6.1** Verify that session lifetime and termination between Relying Parties (RPs) and Identity Providers (IdPs) behave as documented, requiring re-authentication as necessary such as when the maximum time between IdP authentication events is reached. | L2 | fail |  | Not met. The OIDC session is independent of the provider after login (no maximum IdP authentication age, no back-channel logout) and nothing documents this; it also has no absolute lifetime (7.3.2). Tracked in #9007. |
| **7.6.2** Verify that creation of a session requires either the user's consent or an explicit action, preventing the creation of new application sessions without user interaction. | L2 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.6.2]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts) | A session starts only from a credentials POST or from an OIDC callback bound to a login that this browser started with an explicit POST; registration, reset and verification start none. |
